title: Automated operator heal and incremental Helm rollout for on‑prem upgrade failures
creator: Sophie Nguyen
description:
Summary:
Several customers running Private/VPC deployments experienced operator failures during recent Helm-based upgrades. Failures manifest as mixed CR state (some CustomResources stuck in Terminating / Pending) caused by a race between post-upgrade webhooks and leader election transient restarts. In multiple cases config drift (encrypted annotations rotated differently between control plane and nodeagents) prevented automatic reconciliation.

Root cause analysis (ongoing):
- Helm upgrade post-hook triggers mutating/admission changes while operator leader lease is briefly lost during the node restart window.
- Operator does not currently have an idempotent healing path for partially-migrated CRs; helm rollback is often blocked because finalizers remain, resulting in stuck releases.
- Drift in opaque ConfigMaps / secrets between control plane and nodeagent manifests causes webhook rejections when controller reconciles updated schemas.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Implement an automated "operator-heal" subcommand that can safely detect and repair common post-upgrade states (clear stale finalizers when safe, re-run migration reconciliation, and reset broken leader leases).
2) Add an incremental Helm rollout orchestration mode: batch upgrades by namespace/pool with health probes and automated slow-down on errors.
3) Add config-drift detector that compares critical opaque config checksums across control plane and nodeagents and emits actionable alerts + optional auto-sync for low-risk keys.
4) Deliver a hotfix release and customer runbook for manual remediation while the automation rolls out.

Acceptance criteria:
- operator-heal subcommand available in CLI and operator image, documented in runbook; dry-run mode shows proposed actions without mutating.
- Incremental Helm rollout strategy integrated into installer: configurable batch size, health probe thresholds, and safe backoff policy.
- Drift detector emits events and metrics (metric names prefixed redwood.operator.drift) and supports a single-key auto-sync toggle per cluster.
- End-to-end integration tests simulating webhook leader-loss produce no stuck Helm releases in >95% of trials (target improvement from baseline ~40% failure to <5%).
- Customer-facing runbook with scripted kubectl commands and safe-rollback steps published.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Strong preference for opt-in auto-sync for opaque secrets (security posture), with default behavior: alert-only. Customers can enable auto-sync via cluster annotation.
- operator-heal will avoid any mutation that would lose user data; finalizer removals are only performed if the owning controller pod is confirmed absent for >5 minutes and object age > 10m. This increases safety but delays recovery in some cases.
- Incremental rollout increases update latency for large fleets; default batch size tuned to minimize customer impact while preserving availability.
- We considered a strict two-phase upgrade (drain -> upgrade -> restore) but rejected due to customer environments where drain is not feasible (low-margin workloads).

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Add drift checksum collector, expose metrics, and add runbook alert examples.
- Week 2: Implement operator-heal dry-run and surgical repair primitives in controller; add unit + integration tests.
- Week 3: Add Helm orchestrator with batching controls and health probe hooks; run canary on internal staging clusters.
- Week 4: Hotfix release build + customer runbook, coordinate with support for limited early rollout to customers on escalation list.

Artifacts and links:
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Operator+Heal+Runbook
- Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OperatorHealDesign
- Staging PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/981
- Helm orchestrator prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/helm-orchestrator/pull/57

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the safety checks around finalizer removal; propose additional invariants if you know of edge cases that can create data loss.
- UX for the incremental rollout flags should map to Console controls later; keep CLI flags explicit and human-friendly.
